title: Always approved, never held
question: Which firms see their full-review permits put on hold far less often than like permits, pass fewer review stations, or reach issue far more often?
finding: 76% of 17,864 full-review permits issued through 2022 were put on hold at least once, and 78% of full-review applications filed 2012 to 2021 have been issued. Against like permits, 5 of 87 firms tested were held far less often year after year and 0 far more often; 16 of 115 reached issue through at least half a review station fewer than like permits (the average is 4.8); and 2 of 87 saw their applications reach issue far more often. Held least against expectation: Clear Channel Outdoor, on hold on 6% of 50 permits where like permits were held 46% of the time.
how: Full-review alterations and new buildings with drawings. Holds: the City's routing record marks each time a review station put a permit on hold; a permit counts as held if any station did so before issue. That field marks 8.1% of all routing steps in 2021, 6.2% in 2022, 2.9% in 2023 and 0.0% in 2024, so it stopped being filled during 2023 and only permits issued by the end of 2022 are compared. Stations: the number of different technical review stations a permit passed before issue (processing desks left out), for filings 2012 to 2024. Reach issue: full-review applications filed 2012 to 2021 that have been issued, credited to the architects, engineers and agents attached in the first 60 days (contractors are left out: on 53% of full-review permits the first contractor was attached more than 60 days after filing). Each is set against like permits of the same type, review path, cost band and filing year, with the same floors as the speed test and cuts set so that about 0.05 firms per test would pass by luck (3.4, 3.5 and 3.4 standard errors). Listed: held or issued at least 10 points away from like permits, or at least half a station fewer, in three quarters of active years.
limits: A hold can be the applicant's own pause: waiting for a client, a lender, or a separate approval. Complete drawings may draw fewer holds. Fewer stations may simply mean simpler work inside the same cost band, work that fewer departments need to see. An application that never reaches issue may have been dropped by its owner; the records do not say who gave up. Whether a permit was sent back with comments is recorded only from mid-2023, too short a run for a year-after-year test, so that measure is not used. Few firms file 40 full-review permits, so this screen can only see the largest offices.

rows.meets: held far less often; fewer review stations

rows.firm: Comstock Crosser & Assoc Develp Co Inc.
